cover letter
Bachelor's degree in biology or bioengineering, or a related field and/or equivalent training or experience. (Required)
PhD degree in biology or bioengineering or related field and/or equivalent training or experience. (Preferred)
Extensive experience with mouse models, including precise intracranial injections, pre- and post- op surgery experience, and animal handling.
Experience working with a large-scale lab, good communication skills and excellent study management and interpersonal skills.

The Staff Research Associate 3 serves under the direction of Professor David Schaffer, Director of QB3 and Bakar Labs. This position is responsible for overseeing all animal work in the lab, including the design of animal experiments and the creation of original plans for each phase of animal projects. The Staff Research Associate 3 conducts highly technical and physically precise animal surgeries, orders and maintains animal colonies, interprets data yielded by animal studies, and prepares complete written reports on all phases of laboratory animal studies.
Animal Study Management and Planning - 20%
This position will help ensure that the Schaffer Lab is run efficiently through diligent oversight of all animal studies in the lab.

Additionally, proper animal management will include following Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) guidelines, regulations, protocols, and policies that are imperative to safely operating a scientific research facility.

They will initiate and be proactive in anticipating future problems, identifying current challenges and developing and implementing creative and innovative solutions, with follow-up to ensure the continued success of such solutions.

The candidate will be responsible for conducting experiments involving intraparenchymal injections of adeno associated viral preparations to conduct selection and validation experiments of candidate cell type specific AAV vectors.
These are extremely precise procedures that require experienced and masterful technique.
This position will order all animals, determining what genetic strain, sex, and age are required for each experiment.
They will be responsible for ensuring that animals are ready for experiments by monitoring their weight, health, and other vitals.
Animal Study Pre/Post-op Care - 20%

This position will be responsible for all pre- and post-operation care for surgical procedures, including checking on all animal's weight, vitals, and health and determining if any additional care is required.
Communication and Analysis - 10%

Timely, well-messaged, and routine communication is crucial to maximizing work efficiency and organizational cohesiveness, as well as developing an awareness and support of activities associated with the Schaffer Lab.

This position will be able to inform all parties of the current animal experiments that are being conducted and what will need to be conducted in the future, and has the experience to provide guidance for other lab members.
The candidate will be additionally responsible for maintaining general laboratory protocols, including a detailed experimental notebook of procedures and outcomes.
The candidate will maintain regular communication with team members and key collaborators and report on experimental plans, timelines, and results.

This position will also synthesize adeno associated viral preparations which will be used to conduct selection and validation experiments of candidate cell type specific AAV vectors within animal studies.
Grant Proposal Support - 5%
Help compose scientific components of large-scale grant proposals submitted for the PIs proposals, adhering to University and funding agency guidelines.
Reporting Activities - 5%
Help coordinate and author scientific portions of all progressive and end-of-project reporting activities for contracts and grants to fulfill agency requirements.

Proficiency in synthesizing adeno-associated virus (AAV) preparations combined with high-precision surgical techniques to independently conduct, evaluate, and validate candidate cell-type-specific viral vectors in animal models.

Demonstrated capability to oversee the complete lifecycle of animal research projects—spanning strain/specimen procurement, daily physiological monitoring, precise intracranial/intraparenchymal microinjections, and comprehensive pre-/post-operative care—while maintaining strict adherence to EH&S guidelines and regulatory compliance.
Excellent analytical and organizational skills.
